note: Single source of truth: scripts/score_xiii.py evaluates exactly these expressions and scripts/render_predictions.py renders the document table from this file. Thresholds were set on DEVELOPMENT models only (xP81, yP130, vP150, vP155, vP156 and the XII/XI dev pool); confirmation units are the fresh cohort uP160-uP165 (full_c1, seed 20).

predictions.title: Layer-2 attention-mixture (ATT-MIX): inserting a same-question donor's natural mixture-head attention row changes the output as the donor's Bayes responsibilities predict, and better than alternative weightings
predictions.rationale: Class II natural-activation intervention (donor rows are real activations of another natural episode). Development: R2(Bayes) 0.69-0.98, slope 0.95-0.97; shuffled R2 <= 0.002; on donors whose E and A1 eligibilities differ, R2(Bayes) 0.97-0.99 vs R2(A1) 0.17-0.19.

arms.text: fidelity to donor Bayes responsibilities: R2 >= 0.6 and slope in [0.4, 1.25]
Bayes responsibilities beat the separable-discount alternative A3 by >= 0.05 R2
on donors with E != A1 eligibility, Bayes(E) responsibilities beat perfect-only (A1) responsibilities by >= 0.3 R2
validity: re-inserting the model's own rows changes nothing (noop <= 1e-4)

predictions.title: Natural mediation through mixture-head attention: in the TRUE factorial the mixture-head rows mediate far more of the eligibility effect than in the CTRL factorial and than size-matched non-mixture heads
predictions.rationale: Class I input edit (TRUE: eligibility-changing edit; CTRL: matched edit that leaves eligibility unchanged) crossed with class II activation transplant of mixture-head rows. Development: DiD 0.32-0.88 (CI lower bound >= 0.27 in all four), decoy-head/mixture NIE 0.01-0.33, ATT-MIX fidelity of the transplant 0.52-0.98.

arms.text: difference-in-differences of |NIE| (TRUE - CTRL): 95% CI lower bound >= 0.2
mixture heads' TRUE |NIE| >= 0.2 and decoy (non-mixture) heads mediate <= 0.4 of it
the transplanted change follows ATT-MIX predictions: R2 >= 0.45

predictions.title: The mixture-head score contrast that excludes ineligible groups is carried by the E coordinates at layer 2, not by a random subspace or the complement, but matched-budget decoy subspaces (A1, PERM) are NOT specific under mean patching
predictions.rationale: Class III synthetic patch (mean patch of a subspace). Development (xP81, yP130, vP155, vP156): E mean patch removes 1.37-1.47 of the S=1 contrast, random 6-dim <= 0.013, complement makes it more negative; matched decoys A1 and PERM also remove 0.88-1.43 (xP81, vP155). Arm c is therefore a predicted NON-specificity (a diagnostic limitation of mean patching).

arms.text: E-subspace mean patch removes >= 0.8 of the S=1 score contrast
complement (442-dim) mean patch removes <= 0.2 of it
matched-budget decoys are not specific: both A1 and PERM subspace mean patches remove >= 0.5

predictions.title: Layer 2 does not reconstruct eligibility: after layer-1 mean ablation the mixture-head attention loses its alignment with Bayes responsibilities, although eligibility remains linearly decodable outside the E coordinates
predictions.rationale: Class III (mean ablation) plus decoding. Development (xP81, yP130): intact corr(mass, B) 0.95-0.98, after ablation ~0; e decodable from E and from the complement at 1.0; Bayes decision decodable from the complement 0.81-0.92 but not from E (0.41).

arms.text: intact corr(mixture mass, Bayes responsibility) >= 0.8 and after layer-1 mean ablation <= 0.3
redundancy: e_g0 decodable from the complement of E at >= 0.95
the Bayes decision is better decoded from the complement than from E by >= 0.2

predictions.title: Two-colluder repair (C=2) is local to layer 2: with layers 0-1 frozen, adapting layer-2 attention alone or layer-2 MLP alone recovers the exact C=2 posterior including the J_H-dependent S=3 slice, whereas readout-only adaptation does not recover it overall -- although the frozen C=1 resid2 already supports most S=3 decisions linearly
predictions.rationale: Selective adaptation on frozen resid2 (adapt_sel.py, 1000 steps, C=2, beta=1). Development (xP81, vP155): native acc 0.33 (Bayes 0.79); attn-only 0.80/S3 0.97; mlp-only 0.79-0.80/S3 0.92-0.97; full 0.80-0.80/S3 0.97, KL 0.003-0.005; readout-only 0.60-0.64, KL 0.45-0.49, but S3 0.79-0.89 (chance 0.34, native 0.33).

arms.text: the C=1-trained network fails on C=2: native acc <= Bayes acc - 0.2
layer-2 attention-only AND layer-2 MLP-only adaptation each reach acc >= Bayes - 0.03 and S=3 acc >= Bayes(S=3) - 0.1
readout-only adaptation is insufficient overall: KL >= 0.2 and acc <= Bayes - 0.1
the frozen C=1 resid2 already supports the J_H-dependent slice linearly: readout-only S=3 acc >= 0.7
validity: parameters outside each condition are bit-identical after training

predictions.title: EXPLORATORY heterogeneity: parents whose pretraining stayed incomplete after the gate are mixture-class
predictions.status: exploratory (not counted among the primary predictions)
predictions.rationale: Development: all 5 incomplete parents were mixture-class; complete parents split 6 mixture / 5 pre-assembled. Readiness gating is expected to leave few or no incomplete parents, in which case this is inconclusive.

arms.text: mixture-class rule holds

predictions.title: In mixture-class parents, the dominant mixture head's per-group attention mass correlates with Bayes responsibilities (>= 0.8) more than with the A3 alternative (by >= 0.08) and with eligibility-count M (by >= 0.2)
predictions.rationale: Class II correlational (natural episodes). Development: dominant head corr(B) 0.70-0.99 (>= 0.8 in 13/15 mixture-class models), B - A3 0.11-0.14, B - M 0.3-0.4.

arms.text: corr(mass, B) >= 0.8
corr B - corr A3 >= 0.08 and corr B - corr M >= 0.2

predictions.title: Matched-budget subspace interchange (DAS) is NON-identifying between E and A1 but rejects the group-permuted rule: on E != A1 pairs each trained subspace follows its own training rule; on all discriminating pairs E- and A1-trained subspaces follow E far better than PERM
predictions.rationale: Class III synthetic interchange of matched subspaces (das_decoy.py: identical procedure and budget). Development (xP81, vP155): E≠A1 stratum: E-subspace R2(E) 0.35-0.45 vs R2(A1) 0.12-0.14; A1-subspace R2(A1) 0.29-0.44 vs R2(E) 0.06-0.15; all pairs: E-subspace R2(E) 0.93-0.94 vs R2(PERM) 0.00-0.01; random <= 0.04.

arms.text: E != A1 stratum: E-subspace R2(E) - R2(A1) >= 0.1
E != A1 stratum: A1-subspace R2(A1) - R2(E) >= 0.1 (non-identifiability)
